models.title: Horse
models.description: An animated horse galloping at full speed. Horses were domesticated around 3500 BCE and transformed human civilization — enabling faster travel, trade, agriculture, and warfare across ancient cultures worldwide.

models.title: Parrot
models.description: An animated parrot in mid-flight. Parrots have fascinated humans for millennia — ancient Greeks and Romans kept them as exotic pets, and they appear in the writings of Aristotle. Known for intelligence and the ability to mimic speech.

models.title: Flamingo
models.description: An animated flamingo in flight. These striking pink birds have inspired art and mythology since ancient Egypt, where they were associated with the sun god Ra. Their pink color comes entirely from the pigments in the food they eat.

models.title: Stork
models.description: An animated stork in flight. Storks have been symbols of good luck, new life, and fertility across European and Middle Eastern cultures for thousands of years. They were sacred to the Ancient Romans and appear throughout mythology.

models.title: Red Fox
models.description: An animated red fox. Foxes appear in the folklore of nearly every culture on Earth — from Aesop's fables in ancient Greece, to the cunning kitsune of Japanese mythology, to Native American trickster tales. One of the most adaptable mammals on the planet.

models.title: Duck (Classic glTF Model)
models.description: The rubber duck — the most famous test model in 3D graphics history. Originally created by Sony in 2001 to test the glTF file format, this duck has been rendered by virtually every 3D graphics engine in the world. A landmark artifact of the digital age.

models.title: Oil Lantern
models.description: A highly detailed oil lantern representing pre-industrial lighting technology. Before electricity, oil lanterns like this were essential for nighttime work, navigation at sea, and lighting city streets. They symbolize the age of exploration and early industrialization.

models.title: Antique Camera
models.description: A replica of an antique view camera — the technology that revolutionized how humanity documents itself. The invention of photography in the 1830s changed art, science, journalism, and human memory forever. This style of bellows camera was standard from the 1850s through early 1900s.

models.title: Avocado
models.description: A photorealistic avocado. The avocado was cultivated in Mesoamerica as far back as 5,000 BCE — one of the oldest domesticated foods in the Americas. The Aztec word for avocado was 'ahuacatl', and it was considered sacred due to its rich nutrition.

models.title: Toy Car
models.description: A highly detailed toy car with physically-based rendering materials. Toy vehicles have been found in archaeological digs across the ancient world — from clay carts in the Indus Valley (2500 BCE) to wheeled toys in pre-Columbian Mexico. Play is a universal human experience.

models.title: Walking Person
models.description: An animated human figure in mid-stride. Humans are the only species to walk fully upright on two legs — a trait that freed our hands for tools, shaped our anatomy, and defined our evolutionary path. This figure represents every person who has ever explored, discovered, or built something.

models.title: Expressive Robot
models.description: An animated robot capable of expressing emotion. Robots represent humanity's dream of creating artificial life — from the ancient Greek myth of Talos (a mechanical giant), to Leonardo da Vinci's mechanical knight, to today's AI. This robot can wave, dance, and even look sad.
